_meta.framework: Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills — English Language Arts and Reading
_meta.reviewNote: Plain-language paraphrases for teacher display. Grade 5 = §110.7; K–2 = §110.2 (K), §110.3 (1), §110.4 (2); middle school = §110.22 (6), §110.23 (7), §110.24 (8); high school = §110.36 (English I), §110.37 (English II). The (b)(2)/(c)(2) vocabulary strand: 'the student uses newly acquired vocabulary expressively.' First checked 2026-09-17 against Cornell LII (grade 8 (b)(2)(C) also against Texas Gateway). 2026-10-28: the full knowledge-and-skills text of §§110.2, 110.3, 110.4, 110.22, 110.23, 110.24, 110.36, 110.37 (plus 110.38/110.39, not yet stored) was compared word-for-word between TEA's currently-in-effect ch110a/ch110b/ch110c.pdf and Cornell LII — no substantive differences (only line-break hyphenation and LII character-encoding of accented French words). The earlier single-source CAVEAT on grades 6 and 7 is CLEARED; every code in this file is now TWO-SOURCE. Note: the TEKS text itself does not use the word 'cognates' — cognate awareness is an ELPS/cross-linguistic strategy layered onto the context and roots expectations.
